blocks.html: Survival analysis studies time-to-event data: how long it takes for an event (death, relapse, recovery, dropout) to happen, when some subjects have not yet had the event by the time their follow-up ends. This chapter first shows why ordinary regression fails on such data (§14.1–14.3), then builds the survival curve (§14.4), the test that compares curves (§14.5), and the regression model for the hazard (§14.6). A worked analysis of a CBHI dropout cohort (§14.7) and the problem of competing events (§14.8) close it. Any research question phrased as “time until X”, such as time to treatment default or time to scheme dropout, belongs here.
